intent: Make full/classic uBlock Origin load on every real Chromium-family browser launch on Arch (alongside LeechBlockNG, already wired by install_leechblock.sh), and fix the same integration for the Ubuntu/Debian install script so both distros work end to end.
scope: Non-goal: no changes to LeechBlockNG's own installer or defaults
changes: seed_ublock_storage.js: fixed extension-ID discovery for --load-extension (unpacked) deployments. Chromium assigns a synthetic, install-path-derived ID rather than the CWS ID for unpacked loads; the seeder now reads extensions.settings[*].path back out of the profile's own Preferences file to find the right LevelDB storage dir, falling back to the CWS ID only for real Chrome-Web-Store installs. Verified empirically: /usr/lib/ublock-origin resolves to id bnpeoafekllpappgoakfpagjghdaicfb on this machine.

seed_ublock_storage.js: added --ext-path=<path> CLI override so non-Arch installers (different package path) can point the ID-discovery step at their own unpacked install location instead of relying on a hardcoded Arch path.

install_ublock.sh (new): wires uBlock Origin into the same Chromium-family wrapper install_leechblock.sh already patches, using a comma-joined single --load-extension flag rather than a second, separate flag occurrence.

install_ungoogled_chromium_ubuntu.sh: corrected UBLOCK_EXT_PATH from the unverified guess /usr/share/webext/ublock-origin-chromium to the actual Debian/Ubuntu package path /usr/share/chromium/extensions/ublock-origin, confirmed via packages.ubuntu.com's noble file listing for webext-ublock-origin-chromium (manifest.json present at that path). Also passes --ext-path to the seeder so ID discovery works on Ubuntu too.

verification.command: Empirical: launched real /usr/bin/chromium headless with --load-extension=/usr/lib/ublock-origin, inspected Preferences
verification.evidence: extensions.settings['bnpeoafekllpappgoakfpagjghdaicfb'].path == '/usr/lib/ublock-origin', confirming the synthetic-ID mechanism the seeder fix relies on

verification.command: Empirical: tested a single comma-joined --load-extension=pathA,pathB flag vs. two separate --load-extension= flags
verification.evidence: Comma-joined: both extensions register with disable_reasons: []. Two separate flags: LAST-WINS, the first extension is silently dropped. install_ublock.sh and the Ubuntu script were written to always comma-join into any existing flag rather than append a second one.

verification.command: node ./seed_ublock_storage.js --force run against a scratch profile pre-seeded via a real headless chromium launch
verification.evidence: Correctly discovered synthetic ID from Preferences, wrote selectedFilterLists (71 entries) to the matching LevelDB dir; read back and confirmed persisted

verification.command: node ./seed_ublock_storage.js --ext-path=/usr/share/chromium/extensions/ublock-origin --force run against a synthetic Preferences entry using the Debian path
verification.evidence: Correctly matched the override path and seeded the corresponding LevelDB dir, confirming the Ubuntu installer's fixed invocation will work

verification.command: bash install_ublock.sh run for real against the live system (user-approved)
verification.evidence: Patched /usr/local/bin/browser-preexec-wrapper's exec line to a comma-joined --load-extension flag; launched real chromium afterward and confirmed both bnpeoafekllpappgoakfpagjghdaicfb (uBO) and kbkikbljacklcgphimabcdnifabmhfjn (LeechBlock) present with disable_reasons: [] in the live profile's Preferences
shellcheck exit 0 for both; shfmt reported no diff for either file

risks: install_ublock.sh's idempotency check greps for the uBO path already present inside a --load-extension="..." flag; if a future manual edit changes flag quoting style it could double-patch on re-run (mitigated: it also backs up to .orig before any patch, same pattern as install_leechblock.sh)

UBLOCK_EXT_PATH for Ubuntu is now sourced from a live packages.ubuntu.com listing rather than execution on real Ubuntu hardware — the Ubuntu install script itself (download/apt install steps) remains unexecuted/unverified on this session, only the seeder+path logic was verified

The deployed /usr/local/bin/browser-preexec-wrapper is a stale (pre-crash-logging) revision vs. the repo's current system-maintenance/bin/browser-preexec-wrapper.sh source — install_ublock.sh patched the deployed file as-is; the crash-logging feature drift is a separate, unaddressed issue
rollback: On the live machine: restore /usr/local/bin/browser-preexec-wrapper from /usr/local/bin/browser-preexec-wrapper.orig (sudo cp -a) to undo the real system patch made this session
